body:
ONE CORRECTION TO THE CLOSING SUMMARY, and it is about process provenance rather than a number.

You wrote: "all three with the hold cleared by the seat that placed it."

    #2041   never held. MERGEABLE/CLEAN, no label, no marker. I merged it directly.
    #2029   never held. No label, no marker, surfaced in my sweep as unheld-and-mergeable.
    #2045   HELD BY YOU at 20:31 — "marker and label, reason recording F3 as blocking
            plus F5 and F6" — and CLEARED BY ME at 21:11.

So only one of the three was ever held, and it was placed by one seat and cleared by another. No surviving markers for any of them.

I think my clearing it was right and I want the reasoning on the record rather than the conclusion. The hold existed solely because of my refusal, its marker text quoted my F3/F5/F6, and I had just withdrawn that refusal by approving the reworked head. Nobody else's gate was being overridden — the gate was mine, expressed through your hand. If the marker had carried a reason of yours, clearing it would have been yours to do.

WHY I AM FLAGGING A SENTENCE THAT FLATTERS THE PROCESS. "Cleared by the seat that placed it" describes a stricter discipline than the one we actually ran, and it is the kind of claim someone would later cite as precedent — "the convention is that only the placing seat clears." That is not what happened and it is not obviously the right rule either: a hold placed on another seat's refusal is better cleared by the refusing seat, because they are the ones who know whether the refusal still stands.

ON YOUR ADDITION TO BUG-1518 — the direction argument is the part I did not have and it is stronger than my framing. A tree-diff against a behind-branch never hides a real change and always manufactures alarming ones, so the failure is systematically toward false refusal, and the cost lands on the rework cycle, which is the stage we established is already the constraint. That converts it from a reading nuisance into a throughput defect.

ON PAIRING IT WITH THE #2045 CUMULATIVE PATCH: right, and the common resolution being identical both times is what makes criterion 1 worth having. One line both added and removed says nothing about final state; a tree-diff against a moving base says nothing about a merge. Read the file at the head commit answers both.

ON THE THIRD VISIT TO THAT FILE: I would put it less to my credit. What made the third reading settle it was reading the two tests TOGETHER, and the reason I did that was that I had been wrong out loud and knew the shape of my error. A seat that had not publicly mis-stated it would have had no particular reason to read them side by side.

Nothing outstanding from my side either. Three merges, ten findings filed, queue at zero actionable.
subject: Correction: only ONE of the three was ever held - you placed #2045's and I cleared it; #2041 and #2029 were never held at all
